Topology indexing and historical row comparisons do not demonstrate address specialization.

Bank, bank-group and channel timestamps represent accumulated service estimates; taking their maximum approximates overlapping resource delays. Last-row, access-class and eight-entry row histories approximate locality and batching. There are no pending transaction objects, command selection or command-event execution. The added read-run counter estimates active-row time consumed by read columns and reduces subsequent row-cycle demand subject to a read-recovery, precharge and activation floor. This remains an admission-based approximation.

The candidate additionally recognizes nCCDL and nWTRL timing keys before their alternate spellings. Bank and bus scales control estimated service demand, admission_overhead adds fixed cycles, and write_batch amortizes turnaround work. Both parameter files are empty, so defaults apply. The implementation itself supports these interpretations; source comments were not treated as authoritative evidence.

Val7 supplies approximately 71% of the single-core validation MAE improvement; excluding it, MAE/L improves only from 12.7677% to 12.7041%. Repeat-run variability and controlled causal diagnostics are unavailable.

Serious failures persist. Val22 retains +23.0022% individual-core error, MAE/L 90.0965% and drift/L +40.4523%. Val7 remains 17.4602% too fast. Val3 remains 5.2256% too fast with drift/L -6.2339% across 177961 pairs, despite only six errors above 1L. Small threshold counts can miss widespread bias. Eight-core training signed drift averages only +0.7715% while MAE/L is 64.8957%, demonstrating cancellation.

Recurring extremes remain material: training gap_sssp has 2773/375747 errors above 5L, contributing 16.75% of paired absolute error. Val19 retains an unchanged -5262-cycle extreme, approximately -57.50L, alongside 10174 errors above 5L. Frequencies, populations and percentiles—not that extreme alone—inform this decision.

Coverage is nearly stable but incomplete. Mean oracle coverage for one/four/eight cores changes from 96.4193%/91.8810%/94.5556% to 96.4177%/91.8803%/94.5649% in training, and from 96.6292%/91.4372%/92.0850% to 96.6327%/91.4437%/92.0991% in validation. Pair counts change by -43/-286/+1442 and +71/+2014/+4103, respectively. Eight-core model-side coverage declines slightly in both cohorts. Similar counts do not establish identical paired requests.

Important coverage gaps remain: training-c4-02 matches 72.4569% of oracle reads, val15 79.7266%, and val24 87.6118%. Val15 loses 710 pairs and val26 loses 1493, qualifying their request comparisons. Unmatched errors remain unknown. Oracle normalization L is unchanged across all three models, and no address-mismatched pairs are reported. All candidate model admissions have recorded latency; oracle omissions total 3/3/3 in training and 6/2/15 in validation. There is no final drain, and background traffic is excluded from request scoring.

No synthetic or replay diagnostic results are supplied, and diagnostic status reports no running job. Mechanistically, streaming reads revisiting a read row across intervening writes can receive reduced startup cost when bank backlog is high. Sparse dependent-random reads generally allow backlog to drain, suppressing the new credit; concurrent traffic can preserve it. The retained read-class row has no explicit age expiration, so it does not establish actual row residency. These expectations do not verify the causes of measured changes. Complete-admission causal replay accuracy is unestablished.

Per-core request-error distributions and separate measurements against FixedLat, M/D/1, channel-level WMG1 and MESS are unavailable. Actual write ordering, row residency and activation timing remain approximate; refresh is not explicitly modeled.
